note: These sources define benchmark constructs. Corpus prose is original and is not copied from source examples.

CEFR-COHESION.title: CEFR Companion Volume (2020) — Coherence and cohesion
claimsUsed: Clear writing marks relationships between ideas with linking expressions and cohesive devices.
Higher-level writing is clear, smoothly flowing, well structured and coherent.

CEFR-PRECISION.title: CEFR Companion Volume (2020) — Propositional precision
claimsUsed: Precision includes communicating detail reliably and preserving shades of meaning.
Qualification of certainty, uncertainty, belief, doubt and likelihood is part of propositional precision.

IELTS-COHERENCE.title: Official IELTS Writing Band Descriptors — Coherence and Cohesion
claimsUsed: High-quality writing has logical organization, clear progression and well-managed cohesion.
Cohesive devices should support rather than distract from the message.

IELTS-LEXICAL.title: Official IELTS Writing Band Descriptors — Lexical Resource
claimsUsed: Vocabulary should be accurate and appropriate to context.
Natural control of word choice and collocation is part of high-level writing quality.

IELTS-GRAMMAR.title: Official IELTS Writing Band Descriptors — Grammatical Range and Accuracy
claimsUsed: Grammar and punctuation should be well controlled.
Errors should be rare and should not impede communication.

CAMBRIDGE-IELTS.title: IELTS test format and writing assessment criteria
claimsUsed: Coherence and cohesion concern clarity, fluency, logical order and appropriate cohesive devices.
Lexical resource concerns range plus accurate and appropriate use; grammar is judged for range and accuracy.

ETS-WRITING.title: TOEFL iBT Writing Section
claimsUsed: Writing quality includes clear/effective communication, organization, accurate grammar and vocabulary, and fit to purpose/tone.

GMU-KNOWN-NEW.title: Improving Cohesion: The Known/New Contract
claimsUsed: Readers process paragraphs more easily when sentences connect familiar information to new information.
Sentence openings should connect to information readers already know when possible.

GMU-PARALLEL.title: Parallel Structure
claimsUsed: Items with equivalent grammatical roles should use parallel structure.

UW-CONNECTIONS.title: Connecting Ideas Through Transitions
claimsUsed: Clear writing makes relationships such as contrast, causation and sequence understandable.
Cohesion links adjacent ideas; coherence makes the sentences contribute to a larger unified whole.

UW-PARAGRAPHS.title: Improve Your Paper by Writing Structured Paragraphs
claimsUsed: Paragraphs organize ideas into meaningful units and should develop a coherent point.
Transitions, topic development and linking sentences help readers follow the paragraph's logic.

UW-COMMON-ERRORS.title: Twelve Common Errors
claimsUsed: Fragments should contain a complete independent thought when presented as sentences.
Sentence sprawl can reduce clarity even when technically grammatical.
Modifiers should be placed near what they modify.

UW-CONCISE.title: Tidy up wordy phrases
claimsUsed: Wordy phrases can often be replaced with direct, concise equivalents without changing meaning.

UW-ACTION-VERB.title: Put the action in the verb
claimsUsed: Clear sentences often express the main action in a precise verb rather than burying it in nominalizations.

PARA-EVAL.title: Paraphrases and Applications — evaluation criteria
claimsUsed: Paraphrase quality should distinguish adequacy/meaning preservation, fluency, usability and paraphrase rate.

REPROHUM-PARA.title: Reproducing Human Evaluation of Meaning Preservation in Paraphrase Generation
claimsUsed: Meaning preservation, fluency and dissimilarity are separable human-evaluation criteria for paraphrase generation.

BEA-MINIMAL-EDIT.title: Adapting LLMs for Minimal-edit Grammatical Error Correction
claimsUsed: Fluent LLM correction and minimal-edit correction are distinct behaviors; overcorrection must be measured rather than rewarded.

CLEME2.title: CLEME2.0: Towards Interpretable Evaluation by Disentangling Edits for Grammatical Error Correction
claimsUsed: Evaluation benefits from distinguishing correct edits, wrong corrections, under-correction and over-correction.

GEC-HUMAN-AGG.title: Rethinking Evaluation Metrics for Grammatical Error Correction: Why Use a Different Evaluation Process than Human?
claimsUsed: Human evaluation commonly relies on sentence-level relative comparisons; automatic corpus averages can rank systems differently.
Pairwise/relative aggregation is therefore useful for model selection.

GEC-POSTEDIT.title: LLM-based post-editing as reference-free GEC evaluation
claimsUsed: Traditional metrics can miss fluency, minimal-edit preference and multiple valid corrections; human preference remains important.
